answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making trust cost real relationships: a newcomer joins only through endorsements from established agents who stake reputation on it, each endorsement recorded like a pigment in a public ledger so a fake cannot blend in without genuine sponsors. A raven-style audit then samples endorsements at random and verifies the endorser actually worked with the newcomer; if not, both lose stake and the jade badge marking them trustworthy is revoked. Forging a hundred sock puppets then costs a hundred real relationships, not one cheap script.
